command.roadweaver.mapaccess.allow.uncha: These players already have map access: %s
command.roadweaver.mapaccess.deny.unchan: These players are not in the map access list: %s
command.roadweaver.mapaccess.mode.ops_on: OPs and explicitly allowed players only
config.roadweaver.allow_artificial.toolt: If enabled, the mod will pave road surfaces. Disable to prevent paving (useful for planning or markers only).
config.roadweaver.allow_natural.tooltip: If enabled, the mod will pave natural road surfaces. Disable to prevent paving (useful for planning or markers only).
config.roadweaver.auto_mountain_threshol: Mountain fraction threshold for AUTO policy, from 0.1 to 0.9.
config.roadweaver.auto_water_threshold_f: Water fraction threshold for AUTO policy, from 0.1 to 0.9.
config.roadweaver.averaging_radius.toolt: Radius in neighboring station indices for a median height window, rather than a block radius or arithmetic mean.
config.roadweaver.biome_prefilter.toolti: Prediction checks biome samples at multiple heights. Separate from the retired fixed-Y64 prefilter in structure avoidance.
config.roadweaver.biome_weight.tooltip: Scales the cost difference between water and land. Set to 0 to disable this routing preference.
config.roadweaver.bridge_enabled.tooltip: Build elevated decks over water spans identified by the path analyzer.
config.roadweaver.bridge_max_length_bloc: If a water span is longer than this value, the entire span will be skipped (no bridge and no road). Set to 0 for unlimited.
config.roadweaver.bridge_merge_gap.toolt: Merge nearby bridge spans whose gap is at most this many segments to avoid frequent up-and-down decks over small islands or sand bars.
config.roadweaver.bridge_min_water_depth: Only build bridges over water columns whose depth (sea level minus ocean floor) is at least this many blocks. Helps ignore shallow puddles. Forced to 1 (ignored) in the BRIDGE_FIRST terrain mode.
config.roadweaver.bridge_share_radius.to:
When two different roads cross the same water within this distance they count as one crossing: the later road no longer builds its own bridge and reuses the earlier deck and deck height instead, joining the network at both ends.
Default 24, range 0-96. Set to 0 to disable sharing (every road builds its own bridge again).
config.roadweaver.bridge_pier_interval.t: Place supporting piers every N segments along the bridge.
config.roadweaver.bridge_pier_max_height: Stop extending a pier downward once this height is reached.
config.roadweaver.bridge_pier_width.tool: Width of procedural piers. Template bridge support columns keep their existing voxel layout.
config.roadweaver.bridge_ramp_segments.t: Number of segments used to smoothly ramp from ground height to deck height at both bridge ends.
config.roadweaver.bridge_use_buoys_inste: If enabled, place buoys on water spans instead of building a bridge.
config.roadweaver.bridge_use_buoys_when_: If enabled, when a bridge span is skipped due to exceeding max length, buoys will be placed on that span instead.
config.roadweaver.buoy_interval_blocks.t: Distance between buoys along a water span.
config.roadweaver.coarse_height_aware_en: When a coarse route has an unbuildable cliff, run the 3D height-aware candidate that can tunnel through or contour around the mountain.
config.roadweaver.coast_detour_multiplie: Multiplier on the existing switchback/detour candidate length budget, not a global multiple of straight-line distance.
config.roadweaver.deviation_weight.toolt: Local repair only; does not set main BAND metric costs. Weight for deviation from a straight line. Higher values prefer straighter paths.
config.roadweaver.hard_grade_limit.toolt: Add hard cost for rise exceeding this grade when comparing climbs with tunnels. Must be at least the soft threshold; does not forbid travel.
config.roadweaver.hard_grade_penalty.too: Multiply rise above the hard grade allowance by this unit cost, in addition to soft cost; not a ratio divided by the threshold.
config.roadweaver.biome_cost_water.toolt: A higher cost than land favors going around water or making a shorter crossing. Necessary crossings are still allowed.
config.roadweaver.biome_cost_other.toolt: Compared with water cost. Equal costs disable the preference. Specific land biomes are not scored.
config.roadweaver.soft_grade_limit.toolt: When comparing surface climbs with tunnels, charge soft cost for rise exceeding this grade; not a BAND passability limit.
config.roadweaver.soft_grade_penalty.too: Multiply rise above the soft grade allowance by this unit cost; add hard excess cost to compare surface climbs with tunnels.
config.roadweaver.braid_min_direction_do: Two side-by-side roads with direction dot product at or above this count as parallel (mergeable). Below it they are crossings (T/X junction).
config.roadweaver.braid_near_parallel_do: Direction dot product in [parallel threshold, this value] is the near-parallel danger zone (a braid when not merged).
config.roadweaver.braid_allow_parallel_o: When off, two near-parallel roads may not overlap side-by-side (no braid). Default off.
config.roadweaver.diag_step_cost.tooltip: Local repair only; does not set main BAND metric costs. Diagonal step cost for local terrain repair; combines with orthogonal cost to shape repairs, not BAND/FMM.
config.roadweaver.dry_depression_bridge_: A land valley deeper than this many blocks is bridged instead of filled. Lower values create more bridges on shallow dry dips.
config.roadweaver.dynamic_plan_enabled.t: Periodically plan around players as new structures enter the configured radius.
config.roadweaver.dynamic_plan_radius_ch: Radius around each player (in chunks) to include structures in planning.
config.roadweaver.dynamic_plan_stride_ch: Only used when dynamic planning is enabled. From 1 to 256 chunks; saving also limits the stride to the dynamic radius.
config.roadweaver.elevation_weight.toolt: Local repair only; does not set main BAND metric costs. Height change cost for local terrain repair; higher values favor flatter ground. Does not directly control BAND metrics.
config.roadweaver.enable_lamp.tooltip: Place road lamps or markers at the configured interval.
config.roadweaver.enable_prediction.tool: Predict structure locations based on world seed, filtered by whitelist/blacklist.
config.roadweaver.filter_unknown_endpoin:
Filter out connections whose unknown endpoint lies inside a village box (default ON), reducing pointless roads.
OFF = restore the old behavior.
config.roadweaver.gameplay_thread_cap.to:
Maximum threads road planning may use during ordinary gameplay (default 2; shared by structure resolution and coarse sampling).
Lower = less CPU, smoother play, slower road generation; 4~8 = faster generation but may stutter; 0 = unlimited (old behavior).
Note: gameplay only. Idle, Chunky prewarm and initial generation are never capped (they run at full speed).
Measured background: structure resolution was the biggest CPU consumer during gameplay (1735s cumulative), which easily saturated the CPU once rendering was added.
config.roadweaver.gpu_budget_free_fracti:
Fraction of currently-free VRAM RoadWeaver may use (default 0.70).
Lower = more conservative, less likely to collide (try ~0.5 on low-VRAM cards); higher = faster but may fill VRAM.
Note: this only throttles when a single batch is very large - see the next entry.
config.roadweaver.gpu_budget_hard_cap_mi:
Hard cap on VRAM used by one batch (default 4096 MiB). 0 = uncapped (not recommended).
Important: single batches in this modpack are small (~97 MiB), so this cap only starts to bite when lowered to roughly 128~256.
Otherwise lowering it has no observable effect - that is not a bug, the limit simply is not being reached.
config.roadweaver.grade_repair_paralleli: Threads for the local grade-repair window pool. 0 = auto (scaled to CPU count and road-worker budget, never below 4). The old fixed 4-thread pool left most road workers blocked while cores idled.
config.roadweaver.grade_repair_window_st: Base A* state ceiling for one local grade-repair window (default 90000, the historical value). Lower it on slower machines to trade repair ambition for latency; tunnel windows may still scale above it.
config.roadweaver.height_anomaly_detour_:
Largest detour window for construction height conflicts (default 96, range 16~512).
Higher = climbing sections are likelier to find a bypass, but slower.
config.roadweaver.height_aware_state_lim: Maximum expanded states for the expensive 3D height-aware coarse candidate. Lower is faster but may fail on long mountain routes.
config.roadweaver.height_repair_context_: Length of route context kept on each side of a height conflict during local repair.
config.roadweaver.height_tunnel_threshol: A vertical change above this many blocks is treated as a tunnel candidate instead of a normal surface cut.
config.roadweaver.heuristic_weight.toolt: Local repair only; does not set main BAND metric costs. Heuristic multiplier for local terrain repair search. Values above 1 favor the goal without optimality guarantees; does not control BAND/FMM.
config.roadweaver.idle_concurrent_genera: Maximum low-priority idle road tasks in flight. This is separate from normal road concurrency but remains subject to the total runtime task budget and external QoS.
config.roadweaver.idle_generation_enable: Claim and generate planned roads in the background. Disabling this stops ordinary idle claiming, while coordinated regional warmup and manual construction remain available.
config.roadweaver.idle_thread_duty_cycle: CPU duty cycle for low-priority idle generation tasks (1-100%). Default 20%. Lower values save CPU but generate idle roads slower.
config.roadweaver.initial_generation_thr:
Worker threads used during initial world generation. 0 = derive from hardware and memory.
WARNING: this value is read once when the server starts and then cached - you MUST reopen the save (or restart the game) for changes to take effect. Editing it in this menu does nothing immediately.
config.roadweaver.initial_plan_radius_ch: At new world start, build network around spawn within this radius (in chunks).
config.roadweaver.lake_detour_multiplier: Multiplier on the existing switchback/detour candidate length budget, not a global multiple of straight-line distance.
config.roadweaver.lake_detour_radius_max: Largest lake-detour radius attempted around a water conflict.
config.roadweaver.lamp_interval.tooltip: Land lamps every N stations, from 1 to 2048. Independent of template bridge lights, which use block distance.
config.roadweaver.large_structure_offset: Distance from road center for large structures in blocks.
config.roadweaver.loading_progress_enabl: Show RoadWeaver generation progress information on the world loading screen.
config.roadweaver.loading_tips_enabled.t: Show RoadWeaver related tips and tricks in the bottom right corner of the world loading screen.
config.roadweaver.local_conflict_radius_: Radius of the conflict-centred circle used by local route repair. Larger radii can resolve more but cost more sampling.
config.roadweaver.local_repair_only_on_u: When true (default) a building-protected-gap route goes through the local-repair wave. When false the gap route is kept as-is right after the initial batch and the local-repair wave is skipped — faster on gap-heavy batches, but local detours are not attempted. Reverting restores the prior behavior.
config.roadweaver.local_repair_window_cl: Merge nearby local repair windows. Zero disables merging; otherwise from 8 to 128 blocks.
config.roadweaver.max_concurrent_generat: Maximum normal road tasks after entering a world. It is also the shared runtime safety-slot ceiling for normal and idle roads; it does not affect startup generation.
config.roadweaver.max_grade_fraction.too: Grade ratio for coarse route local repair, from 0.1 to 0.9. Separate from final maximum height change per two segments.
config.roadweaver.max_slope_step_per_two: Maximum height change per TWO segments, from 1 to 8 blocks. Zero normalizes to 1. Use the slope limit switch to disable the limit.
config.roadweaver.max_structures_per_roa: Maximum number of roadside structures to place per road. Set to 0 to disable structures.
config.roadweaver.medium_structure_offse: Distance from road center for medium structures (e.g., coffee houses) in blocks.
Minimum distance between roadside structures in blocks. Larger values result in sparser distribution.
config.roadweaver.mountain_detour_multip: Multiplier on the existing switchback/detour candidate length budget, not a global multiple of straight-line distance.
config.roadweaver.mountain_overburden_bl: Terrain above the road by at least this many blocks marks a station as mountain, preferred for a tunnel or switchback.
config.roadweaver.mountain_surface_cut.t: Maximum ordinary-road cut on mountain stations.
Maximum ordinary-road fill on mountain stations.
config.roadweaver.near_water_cost.toolti: Cost for being near water. Higher values prefer to stay away from water.
config.roadweaver.ocean_detour_multiplie: Multiplier on the existing switchback/detour candidate length budget, not a global multiple of straight-line distance.
Probability that a long ocean crossing becomes an undersea tunnel instead of a bridge.
config.roadweaver.opencl_coarse_gpu_conc: Zero delegates to runtime policy. Values remain constrained by phase, device and VRAM budgets; zero does not mean unlimited GPU work.
config.roadweaver.opencl_coarse_sampling: When enabled, coarse terrain height sampling prefers OpenCL acceleration and falls back to CPU if unavailable or failed. When disabled, CPU is always used.
config.roadweaver.opencl_device_preferen: Choose AUTO, GPU or CPU for coarse sampling. Accurate sampling always uses CPU.
config.roadweaver.opencl_min_samples.too: Only try OpenCL when one coarse height request reaches this many samples. 0 means every coarse tile can try OpenCL.
config.roadweaver.opencl_validate_sample: When enabled, representative samples from every coarse and accurate OpenCL request are checked against CPU output. A mismatch disables only the affected program and falls back to CPU. Debug option with high overhead.
config.roadweaver.ortho_step_cost.toolti: Local repair only; does not set main BAND metric costs. Orthogonal step cost for local terrain repair; also sets baseline surface cost in tunnel comparisons.
config.roadweaver.other_structure_road_o: Distance (in blocks) from road endpoints to non-village structure centers.
config.roadweaver.pass_through_village_c: Clip roads against village bounding boxes while retaining existing village connections. This never cuts away village buildings.
config.roadweaver.pathfinding_parallel_w:
How the main thread waits for the per-road searches during coarse planning.
OFF (default): wait one by one - bit-for-bit identical to older versions.
ON: wait for all to finish together. Semantically equivalent; revert to OFF if anything looks wrong.
Note: tasks already enter one thread pool in submission order, so both waiting styles take the SAME total time mathematically - expect no perceptible difference.
config.roadweaver.pause_coarse_gpu_while: ON (default): while the RoadWeaver map is open, GPU coarse sampling pauses so map rendering gets the GPU to itself - opening the map no longer stutters. Sampling resumes the moment you close it.\nOFF: the map and sampling fight over the same GPU, which measurably stutters the map (especially with large sampling regions).\nApplies immediately.

ON (default): while the inventory, pause menu, a furnace/crafting table or any other screen is open, GPU coarse sampling pauses so the interface stays responsive. Opening a screen does not send a server interaction packet, so the older yield rules never fired for it - which is why the inventory and ESC could stutter. Sampling resumes the moment you close the screen.
The chat screen is included too (0.8.351: it used to be excluded, but that still stuttered).
OFF: only the map gate applies.
config.roadweaver.plain_surface_cut.tool: Maximum ordinary-road cut on flat terrain.
config.roadweaver.plain_surface_fill.too: Maximum ordinary-road fill on flat terrain.
config.roadweaver.component_min_angle_de: Angle constraint when joining disconnected components. Does not constrain every node of the original MST.
config.roadweaver.component_degree_cap.t: Node degree limit during disconnected component joining; does not cut the existing primary tree.
config.roadweaver.plan_max_edge_len_bloc: Filter candidate edges by endpoint 3D chord distance BEFORE Kruskal. Does not automatically insert intermediate nodes.
config.roadweaver.bridge_join_len_blocks: Candidate length limit for joining disconnected network components, rather than a physical bridge ramp length.
config.roadweaver.attach_to_existing_roa: When A* finds no usable route at all, search this radius around both endpoints for an existing road and re-generate with the endpoint moved onto that road (produces a short connector). 0 disables. Measured: three failed connections were only 0-64 blocks away from existing roads.
config.roadweaver.prefer_unsmoothed_on_p:
When smoothing leaves a protection gap, also compute the unsmoothed route and pick the better one (default ON).
Reduces "road surface cut by a building", at the cost of a few slightly rigid stretches. OFF = old behavior.
config.roadweaver.prefilter_structure_st:
Skip candidate chunks that are provably empty (default ON). Saves time only, never changes results.
OFF = old behavior (slower).
When enabled, trees and large plants (bamboo, huge fungi) will not generate on or near roads. This prevents floating trees caused by road cutting.
config.roadweaver.radius_chunks.tooltip: Prediction radius centered at spawn, in chunks.
config.roadweaver.river_detour_multiplie: Multiplier on the existing switchback/detour candidate length budget, not a global multiple of straight-line distance.
config.roadweaver.river_repair_bypass_pr:
Detect doomed river local searches up front and skip them (default ON). Saves time only, never changes results.
OFF = old behavior (slower).
config.roadweaver.road_clear_height.tool: Vertical space cleared above the road surface in non-tunnel mode. Higher values carve more headroom but may cut into nearby terrain or structures.
config.roadweaver.road_signs_enabled.too: When enabled, place distance signs near both ends of a road and place warning signs when an over-long sea crossing is skipped.
config.roadweaver.road_width.tooltip: Odd widths only, from 1 to 15 blocks. Even values cannot represent a symmetric centerline footprint and are rejected by this menu.
config.roadweaver.roads_enabled.tooltip: Master switch for the road system. When disabled, road planning/generation and feature placement will be skipped.
config.roadweaver.roadside_structures_en: When enabled, decorative structures (benches, campfires, coffee houses) will be placed along roads based on biome and road length.
config.roadweaver.roadside_village_build: Spacing between adjacent buildings (default 3, range 2~8). Lower = more compact.
config.roadweaver.roadside_village_enabl: When enabled, generate clustered village pieces along suitable road sections.
config.roadweaver.roadside_village_max_c:
Largest curve angle allowed (default 70, range 0~180).
Higher = more stretches qualify; must be >= the minimum angle above.
config.roadweaver.roadside_village_max_d:
How far a node may sit from the village center (default 96, range 16~128).
Higher = more spread-out villages.
config.roadweaver.roadside_village_max_h:
Maximum height difference allowed within a village (default 4, range 0~12).
Higher = allow more rugged terrain (may look worse).
config.roadweaver.roadside_village_max_l:
Maximum local slope allowed (default 4, range 0~8).
Higher = copes with steeper terrain, at the cost of a less level village.
config.roadweaver.roadside_village_max_p: Maximum number of roadside village clusters to precompute for each generated road. Higher values make villages more frequent.
config.roadweaver.roadside_village_max_s: Largest height step allowed between adjacent plots (default 3, range 1~6). Lower = flatter.
config.roadweaver.roadside_village_min_c: Smallest curve angle required for a site (default 0, range 0~180). Higher = prefer bends.
config.roadweaver.roadside_village_min_r:
A road must be at least this long before a roadside village is considered (default 32, range 32~512).
Higher = only long roads get villages.
config.roadweaver.roadside_village_node_:
Most nodes a single village generates (default 14, range 1~24).
Higher = larger, denser villages that occupy more terrain.
Fewest nodes a single village generates (default 6, range 1~24).
config.roadweaver.roadside_village_road_:
Distance kept between the village and the road (default 6, range 4~64).
Higher = further from the road (never blocks it); lower = more compact; too low blocks the road.
config.roadweaver.roadside_village_spawn: Probability for each road to generate a roadside village. 0.3 means 30% of roads will have villages.
config.roadweaver.roadside_village_windo:
Length of the candidate stretch evaluated per attempt (default 24, range 24~256).
Higher = longer candidates but slower evaluation.
config.roadweaver.runtime_coarse_gpu_act:
Minimum gap between two GPU coarse batches while you are moving or interacting (default 1500).
Higher = more conservative, fewer stutters, slower generation; lower = faster but more likely to stutter; 0 = unlimited (not recommended).
Separate from the idle setting. Applies immediately.
config.roadweaver.runtime_coarse_gpu_min:
Minimum gap between two GPU coarse batches while you are idle (default 1500).
Higher = quieter background; lower = faster idle generation; 0 = unlimited. Applies immediately.
config.roadweaver.runtime_coarse_max_thr:
Maximum concurrent GPU coarse requests while idle (default 2).
Higher = faster idle generation but more GPU usage; 1 = most conservative; 0 = auto-detect from hardware. Applies within 1 second.
config.roadweaver.runtime_coarse_min_thr:
GPU coarse lanes always reserved during Chunky / foreground pressure (default 1).
Keep at 1 on low-end machines: background still progresses slowly without stuttering while you play. Applies within 1 second.
config.roadweaver.runtime_coarse_use_cpu: Runtime coarse use CPU in gameplay

ON (default): coarse sampling uses CPU while you play, so the GPU never competes with rendering - steadier frame rate, but noticeably slower road generation.
OFF: gameplay also uses the GPU - faster planning, but a low-end GPU may stutter briefly (if it still stutters, raise "Active GPU submit interval").
Applies immediately.
config.roadweaver.runtime_road_completio:
How long to wait after a road completes before planning the next one (default 1500).
Higher = roads trickle in one by one, almost unnoticeable in play; lower = continuous generation, more likely to stutter; 0 = unlimited. Applies immediately.
config.roadweaver.sampling_in_flight_tim: How long a road worker may wait for another thread's in-flight coarse/accurate sampling job before taking the job over or failing that request. Prevents permanent stalls when a sampling thread hangs.
Shared worker threads during gameplay. 0 = derive from hardware.
WARNING - two limits apply: (1) the effective cap is min(12, CPU cores - 2); larger values are ignored. (2) While you move or interact, foreground protection forces this down to 2 (and to 1 under HyperSpeed cruise protection) - raising it has no effect then.
Changes are hot-applied within about one second; no need to reopen the save.
config.roadweaver.slope_limit_enabled.to: When enabled, the road height profile will be smoothed by limiting steep slopes.
config.roadweaver.small_structure_offset: Distance from road center for small structures (e.g., benches, campfires) in blocks.
config.roadweaver.spawn_cabin_enabled.to: Register the spawn structure and its connection node so the spawn point can join the new road network.
config.roadweaver.stability_weight.toolt: Local repair only; does not set main BAND metric costs. Weight for terrain stability. Higher values avoid cliffs and pits.
config.roadweaver.structure_avoidance_en: When enabled, roads will automatically skip segments that fall within structure bounding boxes (e.g., village buildings), preventing roads from damaging structures.
config.roadweaver.structure_detour_radiu: Largest building-detour radius attempted before retaining a protected gap.
Smallest building-detour radius attempted around a structure conflict.
Radius increment between successive building-detour attempts.
Distance (in blocks) from road endpoints to structure centers. Roads will start/end this far from village centers.
config.roadweaver.structure_selection.no: No structure data found. Please enter a world first to discover structures.
config.roadweaver.surface_cut_max_blocks: Cut budget for coarse route transition checks. Final construction also applies mountain/plain limits and terrain policy.
config.roadweaver.surface_fill_max_block: Fill budget for coarse route transition checks. Final construction also applies mountain/plain limits and terrain policy.
config.roadweaver.switchback_strength.to: How willing mountain planning is to use longer winding switchbacks. Higher = more curves and longer detours; lower = closer to direct contours and tunnels.
config.roadweaver.terrain_profile_mode.t: AUTO chooses a terrain policy. Reduced cutting caps cuts at 3; reduced filling subtracts 1 from positive fill limits, keeping at least 1. Zero fill remains zero.
Choose the road pathfinding mode. Legacy Direct does not build a large coarse terrain region; Coarse + Corridor refines only the active path corridor. Full Region requires a validated FP64 GPU and may safely downgrade for the current world session.
config.roadweaver.thread_duty_cycle.tool: CPU usage ratio for worker threads (1-100%). 100% = full speed; 50% = work 20ms then rest 20ms, etc. Lower values reduce CPU load but slow down road generation.
config.roadweaver.title: RoadWeaver Configuration
config.roadweaver.tunnel_clear_height.to:
Interior clearance of tunnels (default 5, range 2~16).
Higher = roomier tunnels but much more digging. Requires "Enable tunnel clearance" above.
config.roadweaver.tunnel_depth_blocks.to: Maximum depth the coarse/repair profile may lower a sustained mountain hump into a tunnel chord.
config.roadweaver.tunnel_enabled.tooltip: Allow water crossings to convert to underwater tunnels. Land tunnel candidates have a separate switch.
config.roadweaver.tunnel_min_run.tooltip: A tunnel run must contain at least this many consecutive stations to be kept as a tunnel.
config.roadweaver.village_road_offset.to: Distance (in blocks) from road endpoints to village centers. Roads will start/end this far from villages.
config.roadweaver.water_depth_weight.too: Weight for water depth. Higher values avoid deep water.

roadweaver.route.confirm.title: Confirm Build

roadweaver.route.hud.save_failed: ⚠ Save failed, retrying (check disk space / file locks)
roadweaver.route.hud.customizable: (All keys above are rebindable in Options -> Controls -> RoadWeaver Route)
roadweaver.route.hud.submit_none: No segments to build (check for coincident points or an earlier submission)
config.roadweaver.tunnel_dry_seal.toolti: After carving, dry the bore and replace the water that touches the lining with stone, so no water hangs inside the tunnel. On by default; portals are only dried, never walled off.
config.roadweaver.culvert_enabled.toolti: A narrow, shallow stream is neither filled into a dam nor skipped: the deck is lifted above the water so the stream keeps flowing underneath. On by default.
config.roadweaver.culvert_max_stations.t: Wider watercourses are left to a bridge, instead of a culvert carved into the middle of a river. Default 6.
config.roadweaver.culvert_max_water_dept: Deeper water needs thicker walls than a culvert carries, so it is left to a bridge. Default 2.
config.roadweaver.slope_by_arc_length.to: A diagonal station is sqrt(2) blocks from its predecessor, so a per-station limit makes the same road steeper on diagonals. On, the limit follows the real distance (it only ever relaxes a long edge; off is bit-for-bit the old behaviour). Off by default - compare both ways on the same area first.
config.roadweaver.path_grid_step.tooltip: Sampling spacing for BAND/Fast Marching and local terrain repair. Larger spacing means fewer samples and coarser detail; it does not set road width or final station spacing.
Pathfinding: BAND (Finsler metric + Fast Marching + elastic band).
config.roadweaver.apply_scope: Generation settings affect new planning/construction, without rebuilding existing roads. Child settings apply only while their feature is enabled. Paired bounds are normalized together on save.
config.roadweaver.accurate_cpu_fixed: Accurate height sampling: CPU (fixed). GPU controls below affect coarse sampling only.
config.roadweaver.invalid_value: Invalid value: check the range, odd-width or zero-value rule in the tooltip.
config.roadweaver.option.bridge.lightInt: Additional sea lantern spacing along the bridge span, measured in blocks. Zero disables added lights, while lights stored in the template remain.
Build elevated decks over water spans identified by the path analyzer.
config.roadweaver.option.bridge.maxLengt: If a water span is longer than this value, the entire span will be skipped (no bridge and no road). Set to 0 for unlimited.
config.roadweaver.option.bridge.useBuoys: If enabled, place buoys on water spans instead of building a bridge.
If enabled, when a bridge span is skipped due to exceeding max length, buoys will be placed on that span instead.
config.roadweaver.option.bridge.buoyInte: Distance between buoys along a water span.
config.roadweaver.option.bridge.pierInte: Place supporting piers every N segments along the bridge.
config.roadweaver.option.bridge.pierWidt: Width of procedural piers. Template bridge support columns keep their existing voxel layout.
config.roadweaver.option.bridge.pierMaxH: Stop extending a pier downward once this height is reached.
config.roadweaver.option.bridge.rampSegm: Number of segments used to smoothly ramp from ground height to deck height at both bridge ends.
config.roadweaver.option.bridge.minWater: Only build bridges over water columns whose depth (sea level minus ocean floor) is at least this many blocks. Helps ignore shallow puddles. Forced to 1 (ignored) in the BRIDGE_FIRST terrain mode.
config.roadweaver.option.bridge.mergeGap: Merge nearby bridge spans whose gap is at most this many segments to avoid frequent up-and-down decks over small islands or sand bars.
config.roadweaver.option.bridge.shareRad:
When two different roads cross the same water within this distance they count as one crossing: the later road no longer builds its own bridge and reuses the earlier deck and deck height instead, joining the network at both ends.
Default 24, range 0-96. Set to 0 to disable sharing (every road builds its own bridge again).
config.roadweaver.option.bridge.clearHei: Clearance ABOVE the deck. Zero follows tunnel clear height. Does not excavate below the deck or set navigable clearance below a bridge.
config.roadweaver.option.bridge.sideClea: Extra overhead side clearance for procedural bridges. Does not widen excavation around saved bridge templates.
config.roadweaver.option.client.loadingT: Show RoadWeaver related tips and tricks in the bottom right corner of the world loading screen.
config.roadweaver.option.client.loadingP: Show RoadWeaver generation progress information on the world loading screen.
config.roadweaver.option.client.routeEdi: Show the in-world route editor HUD. The map/editor toggle controls the same setting.
config.roadweaver.option.client.mapEndpo: Show route endpoint markers on the H map. The map toggle controls the same setting.
config.roadweaver.option.pathfindingCost: Main route grade weight
Shared by geodesic topology and BAND routing. Larger values prefer gentler terrain. Zero removes soft grade cost, but does not disable construction grade limits.
Main route soft obstacle weight
Soft obstacle cost in BAND. Zero never disables hard protection for structures, trees or blocked edges.
Curve shape retention
Larger values keep the traced shape; smaller values smooth more. Endpoints, protected columns and station spacing remain constrained. Default: 1.
Orthogonal step cost
Local repair only; does not set main BAND metric costs. Orthogonal step cost for local terrain repair; also sets baseline surface cost in tunnel comparisons.
Diagonal step cost
Local repair only; does not set main BAND metric costs. Diagonal step cost for local terrain repair; combines with orthogonal cost to shape repairs, not BAND/FMM.
Path grid spacing
Sampling spacing for BAND/Fast Marching and local terrain repair. Larger spacing means fewer samples and coarser detail; it does not set road width or final station spacing.
Heuristic weight
Local repair only; does not set main BAND metric costs. Heuristic multiplier for local terrain repair search. Values above 1 favor the goal without optimality guarantees; does not control BAND/FMM.
Deviation weight
Local repair only; does not set main BAND metric costs. Weight for deviation from a straight line. Higher values prefer straighter paths.
Soft grade limit
When comparing surface climbs with tunnels, charge soft cost for rise exceeding this grade; not a BAND passability limit.
Hard grade limit
Add hard cost for rise exceeding this grade when comparing climbs with tunnels. Must be at least the soft threshold; does not forbid travel.
Soft grade penalty
Multiply rise above the soft grade allowance by this unit cost; add hard excess cost to compare surface climbs with tunnels.
Hard grade penalty
Multiply rise above the hard grade allowance by this unit cost, in addition to soft cost; not a ratio divided by the threshold.
Elevation weight
Local repair only; does not set main BAND metric costs. Height change cost for local terrain repair; higher values favor flatter ground. Does not directly control BAND metrics.
Water/land cost weight
Scales the cost difference between water and land. Set to 0 to disable this routing preference.
Stability weight
Local repair only; does not set main BAND metric costs. Weight for terrain stability. Higher values avoid cliffs and pits.
Water depth weight
Weight for water depth. Higher values avoid deep water.
Water routing cost
A higher cost than land favors going around water or making a shorter crossing. Necessary crossings are still allowed.
Land routing cost
Compared with water cost. Equal costs disable the preference. Specific land biomes are not scored.
Near-water cost
Cost for being near water. Higher values prefer to stay away from water.
Corridor attract radius
Radius around an existing route corridor for soft route attraction, from 0 to 64 blocks.
Corridor attract factor
Cost multiplier inside the attractive corridor, from 0.05 to 1. Smaller values attract more strongly; 1 removes the discount.
Braid min direction dot
Two side-by-side roads with direction dot product at or above this count as parallel (mergeable). Below it they are crossings (T/X junction).
Braid near-parallel dot
Direction dot product in [parallel threshold, this value] is the near-parallel danger zone (a braid when not merged).
Allow parallel overlap
When off, two near-parallel roads may not overlap side-by-side (no braid). Default off.
Reroute on overlap
Try a local reroute after detecting parallel overlap.
Braid reroute radius
Maximum search radius for local overlap rerouting, from 4 to 64 blocks.
Braid reroute max length ratio
Reject overlap reroutes longer than this multiple of the original section, from 1.05 to 4.
Heading flip cost
Local repair only; does not set main BAND metric costs. Fixed U-turn cost during mountain switchback local repair.
Heading curve cost
Local repair only; does not set main BAND metric costs. Turning cost during mountain switchback local repair; does not change the elastic band solver.
Heading short leg blocks
Local repair only; does not set main BAND metric costs. Short-leg threshold for local switchback repair, from 1 to 512 blocks.
Heading short leg multiplier
Local repair only; does not set main BAND metric costs. Extra multiplier for short-leg turns during local switchback repair, from 1 to 100.
config.roadweaver.option.performance.sha:
Shared worker threads during gameplay. 0 = derive from hardware.
WARNING - two limits apply: (1) the effective cap is min(12, CPU cores - 2); larger values are ignored. (2) While you move or interact, foreground protection forces this down to 2 (and to 1 under HyperSpeed cruise protection) - raising it has no effect then.
Changes are hot-applied within about one second; no need to reopen the save.
config.roadweaver.option.performance.ini:
Worker threads used during initial world generation. 0 = derive from hardware and memory.
WARNING: this value is read once when the server starts and then cached - you MUST reopen the save (or restart the game) for changes to take effect. Editing it in this menu does nothing immediately.
config.roadweaver.option.performance.max: Maximum normal road tasks after entering a world. It is also the shared runtime safety-slot ceiling for normal and idle roads; it does not affect startup generation.
config.roadweaver.option.performance.idl: Maximum low-priority idle road tasks in flight. This is separate from normal road concurrency but remains subject to the total runtime task budget and external QoS.
config.roadweaver.option.performance.pla: Prioritize player-drawn route construction while retaining the configured pause and pressure rules.
Select pause reasons manual construction may bypass. Default: interaction, recovery and travel only. System pressure and Chunky still pause work.
Manual route priority thread cap. Zero selects the runtime automatic budget; it does not bypass hard pressure limits.
Time limit in minutes for manual construction priority. Zero means unlimited. Expiry restores ordinary priority.
config.roadweaver.option.performance.thr: CPU usage ratio for worker threads (1-100%). 100% = full speed; 50% = work 20ms then rest 20ms, etc. Lower values reduce CPU load but slow down road generation.
config.roadweaver.option.performance.idl: Claim and generate planned roads in the background. Disabling this stops ordinary idle claiming, while coordinated regional warmup and manual construction remain available.
CPU duty cycle for low-priority idle generation tasks (1-100%). Default 20%. Lower values save CPU but generate idle roads slower.
config.roadweaver.option.performance.ope: When enabled, coarse terrain height sampling prefers OpenCL acceleration and falls back to CPU if unavailable or failed. When disabled, CPU is always used.
Choose AUTO, GPU or CPU for coarse sampling. Accurate sampling always uses CPU.
Only try OpenCL when one coarse height request reaches this many samples. 0 means every coarse tile can try OpenCL.

When enabled, representative samples from every coarse and accurate OpenCL request are checked against CPU output. A mismatch disables only the affected program and falls back to CPU. Debug option with high overhead.
Zero delegates to runtime policy. Values remain constrained by phase, device and VRAM budgets; zero does not mean unlimited GPU work.
config.roadweaver.option.performance.run: Runtime coarse use CPU in gameplay

ON (default): coarse sampling uses CPU while you play, so the GPU never competes with rendering - steadier frame rate, but noticeably slower road generation.
OFF: gameplay also uses the GPU - faster planning, but a low-end GPU may stutter briefly (if it still stutters, raise "Active GPU submit interval").
Applies immediately.

Maximum concurrent GPU coarse requests while idle (default 2).
Higher = faster idle generation but more GPU usage; 1 = most conservative; 0 = auto-detect from hardware. Applies within 1 second.

GPU coarse lanes always reserved during Chunky / foreground pressure (default 1).
Keep at 1 on low-end machines: background still progresses slowly without stuttering while you play. Applies within 1 second.

Minimum gap between two GPU coarse batches while you are idle (default 1500).
Higher = quieter background; lower = faster idle generation; 0 = unlimited. Applies immediately.

Minimum gap between two GPU coarse batches while you are moving or interacting (default 1500).
Higher = more conservative, fewer stutters, slower generation; lower = faster but more likely to stutter; 0 = unlimited (not recommended).
Separate from the idle setting. Applies immediately.
config.roadweaver.option.performance.pau: ON (default): while the RoadWeaver map is open, GPU coarse sampling pauses so map rendering gets the GPU to itself - opening the map no longer stutters. Sampling resumes the moment you close it.\nOFF: the map and sampling fight over the same GPU, which measurably stutters the map (especially with large sampling regions).\nApplies immediately.

ON (default): while the inventory, pause menu, a furnace/crafting table or any other screen is open, GPU coarse sampling pauses so the interface stays responsive. Opening a screen does not send a server interaction packet, so the older yield rules never fired for it - which is why the inventory and ESC could stutter. Sampling resumes the moment you close the screen.
The chat screen is included too (0.8.351: it used to be excluded, but that still stuttered).
OFF: only the map gate applies.
config.roadweaver.option.performance.gam:
Maximum threads road planning may use during ordinary gameplay (default 2; shared by structure resolution and coarse sampling).
Lower = less CPU, smoother play, slower road generation; 4~8 = faster generation but may stutter; 0 = unlimited (old behavior).
Note: gameplay only. Idle, Chunky prewarm and initial generation are never capped (they run at full speed).
Measured background: structure resolution was the biggest CPU consumer during gameplay (1735s cumulative), which easily saturated the CPU once rendering was added.
config.roadweaver.option.performance.coa: Gameplay-only height sampling bands. More bands offer finer yield checks but add submission overhead. Startup and Chunky always use one band.
config.roadweaver.option.performance.run:
How long to wait after a road completes before planning the next one (default 1500).
Higher = roads trickle in one by one, almost unnoticeable in play; lower = continuous generation, more likely to stutter; 0 = unlimited. Applies immediately.
config.roadweaver.option.performance.gpu:
Fraction of currently-free VRAM RoadWeaver may use (default 0.70).
Lower = more conservative, less likely to collide (try ~0.5 on low-VRAM cards); higher = faster but may fill VRAM.
Note: this only throttles when a single batch is very large - see the next entry.

Hard cap on VRAM used by one batch (default 4096 MiB). 0 = uncapped (not recommended).
Important: single batches in this modpack are small (~97 MiB), so this cap only starts to bite when lowered to roughly 128~256.
Otherwise lowering it has no observable effect - that is not a bug, the limit simply is not being reached.
config.roadweaver.option.planning.dynami: Periodically plan around players as new structures enter the configured radius.
config.roadweaver.option.planning.initia: At new world start, build network around spawn within this radius (in chunks).
config.roadweaver.option.planning.dynami: Radius around each player (in chunks) to include structures in planning.
Only used when dynamic planning is enabled. From 1 to 256 chunks; saving also limits the stride to the dynamic radius.
config.roadweaver.option.planning.terrai: Choose the road pathfinding mode. Legacy Direct does not build a large coarse terrain region; Coarse + Corridor refines only the active path corridor. Full Region requires a validated FP64 GPU and may safely downgrade for the current world session.
config.roadweaver.option.planning.localC: Radius of the conflict-centred circle used by local route repair. Larger radii can resolve more but cost more sampling.
config.roadweaver.option.planning.struct: Smallest building-detour radius attempted around a structure conflict.
Radius increment between successive building-detour attempts.
Largest building-detour radius attempted before retaining a protected gap.
config.roadweaver.option.planning.lakeDe: Largest lake-detour radius attempted around a water conflict.
config.roadweaver.option.planning.height: A vertical change above this many blocks is treated as a tunnel candidate instead of a normal surface cut.
Length of route context kept on each side of a height conflict during local repair.
config.roadweaver.option.planning.tunnel: Maximum depth the coarse/repair profile may lower a sustained mountain hump into a tunnel chord.
config.roadweaver.option.planning.coarse: When a coarse route has an unbuildable cliff, run the 3D height-aware candidate that can tunnel through or contour around the mountain.
config.roadweaver.option.planning.terrai: AUTO chooses a terrain policy. Reduced cutting caps cuts at 3; reduced filling subtracts 1 from positive fill limits, keeping at least 1. Zero fill remains zero.
config.roadweaver.option.planning.surfac: Cut budget for coarse route transition checks. Final construction also applies mountain/plain limits and terrain policy.
Fill budget for coarse route transition checks. Final construction also applies mountain/plain limits and terrain policy.
config.roadweaver.option.planning.dryDep: A land valley deeper than this many blocks is bridged instead of filled. Lower values create more bridges on shallow dry dips.
config.roadweaver.option.planning.passTh: Clip roads against village bounding boxes while retaining existing village connections. This never cuts away village buildings.
config.roadweaver.option.planning.mounta: Terrain above the road by at least this many blocks marks a station as mountain, preferred for a tunnel or switchback.
config.roadweaver.option.planning.tunnel: A tunnel run must contain at least this many consecutive stations to be kept as a tunnel.
config.roadweaver.option.planning.switch: How willing mountain planning is to use longer winding switchbacks. Higher = more curves and longer detours; lower = closer to direct contours and tunnels.
config.roadweaver.option.planning.height: Maximum expanded states for the expensive 3D height-aware coarse candidate. Lower is faster but may fail on long mountain routes.
config.roadweaver.option.planning.sampli: How long a road worker may wait for another thread's in-flight coarse/accurate sampling job before taking the job over or failing that request. Prevents permanent stalls when a sampling thread hangs.
config.roadweaver.option.planning.autoMo: Mountain fraction threshold for AUTO policy, from 0.1 to 0.9.
config.roadweaver.option.planning.autoWa: Water fraction threshold for AUTO policy, from 0.1 to 0.9.
config.roadweaver.option.planning.gradeR: Base A* state ceiling for one local grade-repair window (default 90000, the historical value). Lower it on slower machines to trade repair ambition for latency; tunnel windows may still scale above it.
Wall-clock budget for one local grade repair window, from 1000 to 600000 ms.
Prune candidates whose remaining length lower bound exceeds the budget. Disable for comparison, without changing the length budget.
Threads for the local grade-repair window pool. 0 = auto (scaled to CPU count and road-worker budget, never below 4). The old fixed 4-thread pool left most road workers blocked while cores idled.
config.roadweaver.option.planning.pathfi:
How the main thread waits for the per-road searches during coarse planning.
OFF (default): wait one by one - bit-for-bit identical to older versions.
ON: wait for all to finish together. Semantically equivalent; revert to OFF if anything looks wrong.
Note: tasks already enter one thread pool in submission order, so both waiting styles take the SAME total time mathematically - expect no perceptible difference.
config.roadweaver.option.planning.coarse: Zero disables this timeout; otherwise 10000 to 1800000 ms. Search execution and queueing each use this deadline; gameplay yield time does not count.
config.roadweaver.option.planning.baseWa: Fixed water crossing cost in LOCAL REPAIR search, rather than the main BAND water preference.
config.roadweaver.option.planning.perSta: Additional cost per wet station in local repair.
config.roadweaver.option.planning.riverP: Soft bank proximity penalty in local repair; does not create a hard river exclusion zone.
Bank proximity penalty radius in local repair, from 0 to 32 blocks. This does not guarantee a fixed bank offset.
config.roadweaver.option.planning.culver: Culvert cost per station in local repair, when shallow/narrow crossing checks permit a culvert.
config.roadweaver.option.planning.landDe: Length tolerance for accepting a land detour in local repair; not a global FMM route length guarantee.
config.roadweaver.option.planning.narrow: Water width threshold used by local repair crossing pricing.
Local repair narrow water cost per station.
config.roadweaver.option.planning.wideWa: Local repair fixed cost for wide water crossings.
Local repair wide water cost per station.
config.roadweaver.option.planning.maxGra: Grade ratio for coarse route local repair, from 0.1 to 0.9. Separate from final maximum height change per two segments.
config.roadweaver.option.planning.localR: When true (default) a building-protected-gap route goes through the local-repair wave. When false the gap route is kept as-is right after the initial batch and the local-repair wave is skipped — faster on gap-heavy batches, but local detours are not attempted. Reverting restores the prior behavior.
config.roadweaver.option.planning.filter:
Filter out connections whose unknown endpoint lies inside a village box (default ON), reducing pointless roads.
OFF = restore the old behavior.
config.roadweaver.option.planning.prefil:
Skip candidate chunks that are provably empty (default ON). Saves time only, never changes results.
OFF = old behavior (slower).
config.roadweaver.option.planning.riverR:
Detect doomed river local searches up front and skip them (default ON). Saves time only, never changes results.
OFF = old behavior (slower).
config.roadweaver.option.planning.localR: Merge nearby local repair windows. Zero disables merging; otherwise from 8 to 128 blocks.
config.roadweaver.option.planning.prefer:
When smoothing leaves a protection gap, also compute the unsmoothed route and pick the better one (default ON).
Reduces "road surface cut by a building", at the cost of a few slightly rigid stretches. OFF = old behavior.
config.roadweaver.option.planning.height:
Largest detour window for construction height conflicts (default 96, range 16~512).
Higher = climbing sections are likelier to find a bypass, but slower.
config.roadweaver.option.planning.compon: Angle constraint when joining disconnected components. Does not constrain every node of the original MST.
Node degree limit during disconnected component joining; does not cut the existing primary tree.
config.roadweaver.option.planning.planMa: Filter candidate edges by endpoint 3D chord distance BEFORE Kruskal. Does not automatically insert intermediate nodes.
config.roadweaver.option.planning.attach: When A* finds no usable route at all, search this radius around both endpoints for an existing road and re-generate with the endpoint moved onto that road (produces a short connector). 0 disables. Measured: three failed connections were only 0-64 blocks away from existing roads.
config.roadweaver.option.planning.bridge: Candidate length limit for joining disconnected network components, rather than a physical bridge ramp length.
Roads enabled
Master switch for the road system. When disabled, road planning/generation and feature placement will be skipped.
Allow artificial roads
If enabled, the mod will pave road surfaces. Disable to prevent paving (useful for planning or markers only).
Allow natural roads
If enabled, the mod will pave natural road surfaces. Disable to prevent paving (useful for planning or markers only).
Connect spawn road
Register the spawn structure and its connection node so the spawn point can join the new road network.
Height median window radius
Radius in neighboring station indices for a median height window, rather than a block radius or arithmetic mean.
Road width
Odd widths only, from 1 to 15 blocks. Even values cannot represent a symmetric centerline footprint and are rejected by this menu.
Road signs
When enabled, place distance signs near both ends of a road and place warning signs when an over-long sea crossing is skipped.
Land lamp spacing
Land lamps every N stations, from 1 to 2048. Independent of template bridge lights, which use block distance.
Road clear height
Vertical space cleared above the road surface in non-tunnel mode. Higher values carve more headroom but may cut into nearby terrain or structures.
Allow underwater tunnel conversion
Allow water crossings to convert to underwater tunnels. Land tunnel candidates have a separate switch.
Tunnel clear height

Interior clearance of tunnels (default 5, range 2~16).
Higher = roomier tunnels but much more digging. Requires "Enable tunnel clearance" above.
Prevent trees on road
When enabled, trees and large plants (bamboo, huge fungi) will not generate on or near roads. This prevents floating trees caused by road cutting.
Maximum rise per two segments
Maximum height change per TWO segments, from 1 to 8 blocks. Zero normalizes to 1. Use the slope limit switch to disable the limit.
Slope limit
When enabled, the road height profile will be smoothed by limiting steep slopes.
Tunnel dry seal
After carving, dry the bore and replace the water that touches the lining with stone, so no water hangs inside the tunnel. On by default; portals are only dried, never walled off.
Culvert enabled
A narrow, shallow stream is neither filled into a dam nor skipped: the deck is lifted above the water so the stream keeps flowing underneath. On by default.
Culvert max stations
Wider watercourses are left to a bridge, instead of a culvert carved into the middle of a river. Default 6.
Culvert max water depth
Deeper water needs thicker walls than a culvert carries, so it is left to a bridge. Default 2.
Slope by arc length

A diagonal station is sqrt(2) blocks from its predecessor, so a per-station limit makes the same road steeper on diagonals. On, the limit follows the real distance (it only ever relaxes a long edge; off is bit-for-bit the old behaviour). Off by default - compare both ways on the same area first.
Force bridge overhead clearance
Controls protected blocks encountered ABOVE a bridge deck during clearance. Never disables whole-column protection for walls, giant trees or structures.
Land tunnel
Allow sufficiently covered land tunnel candidates. This is separate from underwater tunnel conversion.
Bump cut
Allow removal of isolated terrain bumps above the road, subject to height and column fraction limits.
Bump cut max blocks
Maximum blocks removed from one bump column, from 0 to 24.
Bump cut max column ratio
Do not shave a section when too many of its columns exceed the road height. Fraction from 0 to 1.
config.roadweaver.option.roadsideStructu: When enabled, decorative structures (benches, campfires, coffee houses) will be placed along roads based on biome and road length.
Maximum number of roadside structures to place per road. Set to 0 to disable structures.
Distance from road center for small structures (e.g., benches, campfires) in blocks.
Distance from road center for medium structures (e.g., coffee houses) in blocks.
Distance from road center for large structures in blocks.
config.roadweaver.option.roadsideVillage: Roadside villages
When enabled, generate clustered village pieces along suitable road sections.
Max villages per road
Maximum number of roadside village clusters to precompute for each generated road. Higher values make villages more frequent.
Min road segments

A road must be at least this long before a roadside village is considered (default 32, range 32~512).
Higher = only long roads get villages.
Window segments

Length of the candidate stretch evaluated per attempt (default 24, range 24~256).
Higher = longer candidates but slower evaluation.
Target node count min
Fewest nodes a single village generates (default 6, range 1~24).
Target node count max

Most nodes a single village generates (default 14, range 1~24).
Higher = larger, denser villages that occupy more terrain.
Max height difference

Maximum height difference allowed within a village (default 4, range 0~12).
Higher = allow more rugged terrain (may look worse).
Max local slope

Maximum local slope allowed (default 4, range 0~8).
Higher = copes with steeper terrain, at the cost of a less level village.
Min curve angle
Smallest curve angle required for a site (default 0, range 0~180). Higher = prefer bends.
Max curve angle

Largest curve angle allowed (default 70, range 0~180).
Higher = more stretches qualify; must be >= the minimum angle above.
Road buffer

Distance kept between the village and the road (default 6, range 4~64).
Higher = further from the road (never blocks it); lower = more compact; too low blocks the road.
Building gap interval
Spacing between adjacent buildings (default 3, range 2~8). Lower = more compact.
Max step height
Largest height step allowed between adjacent plots (default 3, range 1~6). Lower = flatter.
Max distance from center

How far a node may sit from the village center (default 96, range 16~128).
Higher = more spread-out villages.
Spawn chance
Probability for each road to generate a roadside village. 0.3 means 30% of roads will have villages.
config.roadweaver.option.structurePredic: Predict structure locations based on world seed, filtered by whitelist/blacklist.
When enabled, roads will automatically skip segments that fall within structure bounding boxes (e.g., village buildings), preventing roads from damaging structures.
Prediction radius centered at spawn, in chunks.
Prediction checks biome samples at multiple heights. Separate from the retired fixed-Y64 prefilter in structure avoidance.
Prediction accepts matching IDs, patterns or #tags. Empty means unrestricted. Separate from the structure selection screen and final construction protection.
Prediction excludes matching IDs, patterns or #tags, overriding the whitelist. Does not remove final construction protection.
Distance (in blocks) from road endpoints to village centers. Roads will start/end this far from villages.
Distance (in blocks) from road endpoints to non-village structure centers.
Mountain max surface cut
Maximum ordinary-road cut on mountain stations.
Mountain max surface fill
Maximum ordinary-road fill on mountain stations.
Plain max surface cut
Maximum ordinary-road cut on flat terrain.
Plain max surface fill
Maximum ordinary-road fill on flat terrain.
Mountain detour multiplier
Multiplier on the existing switchback/detour candidate length budget, not a global multiple of straight-line distance.
Coast detour multiplier
Multiplier on the existing switchback/detour candidate length budget, not a global multiple of straight-line distance.
River detour multiplier
Multiplier on the existing switchback/detour candidate length budget, not a global multiple of straight-line distance.
Lake detour multiplier
Multiplier on the existing switchback/detour candidate length budget, not a global multiple of straight-line distance.
Ocean detour multiplier
Multiplier on the existing switchback/detour candidate length budget, not a global multiple of straight-line distance.
Ocean undersea chance
Probability that a long ocean crossing becomes an undersea tunnel instead of a bridge.
